name: High Tech Machine
summary: A family-owned precision machine shop in Houston, producing prototypes, complicated parts and production runs for the oil and gas, aerospace, mining and marine industries.

hero.title: Delivering superior quality
hero.lead: High Tech Machine has the industry knowledge and expertise to deliver your machining job right the first time. We machine high-end prototypes, tackle unique setups and produce complicated parts for clients at home and overseas.
hero.imageAlt: A machinist measuring a large machined part with a portable inspection arm

groups.title: Turning and Lathe Work
groups.summary: Manual and CNC turning up to 40 inches in diameter and 120 inches between centers.
groups.intro: HTM's floor is laid out with CNC machining centers and lathes surrounded by complementary manual machines. That mix lets one job run as a single R&D piece and the next run as a large production batch, without moving shops.
groups.imageAlt: A heavy-duty engine lathe on the High Tech Machine shop floor

services.title: CNC Turning
services.text: CNC horizontal and vertical lathes for repeatable parts, from a first article through a full production run.

services.title: Manual Turning
services.text: Manual lathes alongside the CNC machines, for one-off work, rework and setups that are quicker done by hand.

services.title: Subsea and Downhole Components
services.text: HTM specializes in projects for subsea and land-based downhole tools, where tolerance and material certification both matter.

groups.title: Milling
groups.summary: Manual and CNC milling, including four and five-axis programming and machining.
groups.intro: Complex milling is handled both manually and on CNC. HTM offers four and five-axis programming as well as five-axis machining, so a part with features on several faces can be cut in fewer setups.
groups.imageAlt: A part fixtured on the rotary table of a CNC vertical machining center

services.title: CNC Milling
services.text: CNC machining centers for complex milled parts, run from programs written in-house.

services.title: Manual Milling
services.text: Manual mills for fixtures, modifications and short work that does not justify a program.

services.title: Custom Components
services.text: From start to finish, HTM creates and fabricates custom components to a customer's drawings and specifications.

groups.title: Inspection and Finishing
groups.summary: CMM and Romer arm inspection, with an in-house phosphate tank for small parts.
groups.intro: Quality is checked before manufacturing begins and again at the end. Final inspection and testing use calibrated tools, logged and calibrated to NIST standards, so a part leaves only once it meets the requirements set at the start.
groups.imageAlt: Rows of finished machined aluminum components

services.title: Romer Arm Inspection
services.text: Portable arm inspection for large parts and features that cannot be brought to a fixed machine.
points: Measurement on the machine or the bench

services.title: Phosphate Coating
services.text: A small-part phosphate tank in-house, so light finishing does not have to leave the building.

groups.summary: R&D prototypes and full production runs out of the same shop, with no second learning curve.
groups.intro: The floor is arranged so a single piece for R&D prototyping and a large production run can both be executed. Customers can go straight from prototype to production while skipping the learning curve of a new machine shop.
groups.imageAlt: A component being machined with chips cleared to one side

about.title: Quality machining is in our blood.
text: HTM has been a family owned and operated machine shop since 1995. Owners Gary and Melinda Bodukoglu joined Melinda's parents, Rick and Linda Jones, shortly after the company was founded, and together they worked to establish and grow a thriving machine shop. In 2011 Gary and Melinda assumed sole ownership and have continued to invest in innovation and in industry education and training.

Operations are headquartered in a 20,000-plus square foot building in Houston, Texas. Situated on several acres of land, HTM is poised for the future growth and expansion needed to serve its customers.

The team is talented and dedicated. HTM recruits experienced machinists and also invests in its current employees: many started as a shop helper, delivery driver or in deburr and worked their way up to first class machinist, lead man and CNC programmer. More than 40% of employees have been with the company ten years or more.

Customer collaboration and satisfaction are paramount. From the first engagement with engineers through to the way HTM works with its vendors, a high level of teamwork and collaboration runs through the whole machining process, and that is what lets HTM minimize risk, improve performance and reduce costs while ensuring a safe and productive working environment.

faqs.q: What industries does HTM machine for?
faqs.a: Oil and gas, aerospace, mining and marine, along with many others, both domestically and internationally. HTM specializes in subsea and land-based downhole tools.

faqs.q: How large a part can you turn?
faqs.a: Up to 40 inches outside diameter on manual and CNC lathes, and up to 120 inches of bed length.

faqs.q: What materials do you work with?
faqs.a: Inconel, chrome, stainless, carbon steel, forgings, brass, copper, bronze, beryllium, aluminum and duplex. HTM procures the material as part of the job.

faqs.q: Can you take a part from prototype through to production?
faqs.a: Yes. The shop is set up for both one-piece R&D prototyping and large production machining, so customers can move from prototype to production without starting over with a new shop.
HTM is ISO 9001:2015 certified and an accredited Better Business Bureau business. Final inspection uses tools logged and calibrated to NIST standards.

faqs.q: Do you handle processes you do not do in-house?
faqs.a: Yes. Coatings, honing, NDE, EDM, heat treating and welding are turnkeyed through approved suppliers whose quality and on-time delivery are continuously monitored.

facts.heading: Turnkey and Outsourced Services
facts.text: HTM maintains strategic relationships and partnerships so the processes a part needs outside the shop stay part of one streamlined process.

facts.heading: How a Job Runs
items: Project review: requirements and expectations established upfront
System entry: the job gets a unique identification number so every step is monitored
Router creation: a job router sets the order of operations, customer requirements and quality checks
Accuracy check: quality control reviews routers and part specifications before manufacturing begins
Execution: the project moves through departments as the requirements specify
Inspection: final inspection and testing with tools logged and calibrated to NIST standards
Delivery: parts packaged and wrapped to customer specifications

facts.heading: What HTM Commits To
facts.text: High-quality products, unparalleled service and timely delivery, for clients domestically and internationally. HTM has the industry knowledge, experience and expertise to get a project done right the first time.

facts.heading: Quality Statement
facts.text: To produce products and services that meet or exceed our customer's requirements and comply with all statutory and regulatory requirements by adhering to our Management System, Quality Objectives and Operational Methods.

facts.heading: Safety Statement
facts.text: Safety and health are a top priority at High Tech Machine. HTM is committed to working with its employees to provide a safe, accident-free and healthy work environment. The safety policies are based on past experience and current standards, are an integral part of company personnel policy, and compliance with them is a condition of employment.

facts.heading: Environmental Statement
facts.text: HTM accepts its environmental responsibilities and recognizes its obligation to contribute to the resolution of local environmental issues by reducing its environmental impacts. As a manufacturer HTM also takes a leading role in promoting environmental good practice, and so will:
items: Continue to comply with all relevant legislation and codes of practice
Continually seek to improve our environmental performance
Integrate environmental concerns into planning, design, maintenance and management decisions
Improve employee environmental awareness and understanding
Encourage all employees to apply the environmental values we operate by
